description: Use case: the sun intensity, the household electricity price and, where a national figure exists, the feed-in remuneration per country for the photovoltaic return formulas of pv_yield.json, which also holds the general phrases and the self-consumption share; Switzerland is in pv_yield_switzerland.json, because its prices are per municipality. For two sample places per country, selected by their postal code, PVGIS 5.3 gives the yearly global horizontal irradiation, the yearly irradiation on a panel at the optimal slope and the yearly yield of one kWp; the coordinates are those of the postal code in OpenStreetMap. The household electricity price is the national average of Eurostat for the second half of 2025. A feed-in remuneration is stated only where a national figure exists, so all three return formulas apply to these countries and only the return with self-consumption to the others. Austria has no fixed national tariff: the optional OeMAG pays a regulated monthly market price under § 41 ÖSG (5.720 to 10.168 ct per kWh from January to September 2026, OeMAG Marktpreis) and most households sell to a supplier at its contract price. Belgium has no national figure: in Flanders and Wallonia a new installation sells its surplus at the injection tariff of its supplier contract without a statutory minimum (VREG, Service public de Wallonie). In Bulgaria the feed-in remuneration is the preferential price for small rooftop installations set by the Energy and Water Regulatory Commission. Croatia credits the fed-in energy at a factor times the energy price that the household pays itself (ZOIE Art. 51, Narodne novine 78/2025) and this factor is not yet set for households that apply from 2026. Czechia has no regulated price for a new small installation since 2014: the surplus is sold at the price of a supplier contract. A new installation in Denmark gets no price supplement and sells its surplus at the contract price of a production supplier, usually the hourly spot price minus fees (Danish Energy Agency). Estonia has no feed-in tariff and no statutory minimum: the surplus is sold under the contract of the electricity seller, usually linked to the Nord Pool spot price (Elektrilevi). Finland has no statutory tariff: the surplus is sold under a contract with an electricity seller, most commonly at the exchange spot price minus a fee (Motiva). In France the feed-in remuneration is the fixed purchase tariff for the surplus of a small installation set by the decree of 1 June 2026. In Germany the feed-in remuneration is the fixed EEG tariff of the Bundesnetzagentur for a small installation with partial feed-in. A new household installation up to 10.8 kW in Greece is in net billing, where the fed-in energy is paid at the day-ahead market clearing price of each settlement period (Law 5106/2024, as summarised by HELAPCO). A small installation (HMKE) under gross billing in Hungary is paid the universal-service tariff of the 4/2011 NFM decree, which differs by distribution area and could not be pinned to one value. In Italy the feed-in remuneration is the guaranteed minimum price of the Ritiro Dedicato of GSE, which is paid if the hourly zonal market price is lower. Latvia uses net billing at the Nord Pool Latvia price minus at most 20 EUR per MWh and never below 0 (Cabinet Regulation No. 635, point 18.20). Lithuania uses net metering: the fed-in kWh are stored in the grid and taken back for a grid-use fee of the distribution operator ESO. The Netherlands uses net metering (salderen) until the end of 2026, which offsets the fed-in kWh at the full retail price, while the surplus above the own consumption gets a reasonable supplier payment without statutory minimum (ACM). Norway has no national figure: a plusskunde sells the surplus to the own electricity supplier on free-market terms, most commonly at the spot price (NVE). Poland uses net billing: the fed-in energy of a prosumer up to 50 kW is credited to a deposit at the monthly market price RCEm of PSE (e.g. 294.53 PLN per MWh in August 2026), which changes every month. Portugal has no national figure: the surplus is sold to a supplier at its contract price, and the last-resort aggregator pays the hourly OMIE price net of deviation costs and an intermediation fee of ERSE (DL 15/2022). A prosumer up to 200 kW in Romania gets a kWh-for-kWh compensation on the bill at the energy price of the own supply contract (ANRE). Slovakia has no statutory purchase price for a new small installation: the surplus is sold under a private supplier contract, and an installation funded by the Zelená domácnostiam grant delivers it without payment (ZSE). A new installation in Slovenia has no net metering and sells its surplus under the self-supply contract of the supplier at the agreed price (Government of Slovenia, decree on self-supply). The simplified compensation in Spain values the surplus at the hourly price of the daily and intraday market minus the deviation costs and credits it only against the energy bought in the same month (Real Decreto 244/2019, art. 14.3). Sweden has no statutory tariff and abolished the tax reduction of 60 öre per kWh for electricity fed in from 2026 (Prop. 2024/25:109): the income is the spot or contract price of the buyer plus the grid-benefit compensation of the grid company.

sources.name: PVGIS 5.3
sources.description: Photovoltaic Geographical Information System version 5.3 of the European Commission Joint Research Centre, tool PVcalc queried on 8 October 2026 with the default settings: radiation database PVGIS-SARAH3 with the years 2005 to 2023, meteorological data ERA5, horizon shading calculated from the elevation model, crystalline silicon panels with a peak power of 1 kWp and 14 percent system loss, free-standing at the optimal slope and azimuth for the yield and at slope 0 for the global horizontal irradiation.

sources.name: Eurostat electricity prices for household consumers
sources.description: Eurostat dataset nrg_pc_204, electricity prices for household consumers, bi-annual data, queried on 8 October 2026: the national average price of the consumption band DC (2500 to 4999 kWh per year) including all taxes and levies in EUR per kWh, also for the countries outside the euro area; the second half of 2025 is the latest semester with a price for every country.

sources.name: KEVR decision C-8 2026 preferential prices
sources.description: Energy and Water Regulatory Commission of Bulgaria (KEVR), decision No. C-8 of 30 June 2026, item I.1, under Art. 32 para. 1 item 1 of the Renewable Energy Act: from 1 July 2026 the preferential price without VAT for photovoltaic installations up to 30 kWp on roofs and facades of buildings connected to the distribution grid in urban areas is 54.57 EUR per MWh, bought up to a net specific production of 1339 kWh per kWp; the price is set every year by 30 June.

sources.name: Arrêté du 1er juin 2026 photovoltaic purchase tariff
sources.description: Ministère de l'économie, arrêté du 1er juin 2026 modifiant l'arrêté du 6 octobre 2021 fixant les conditions d'achat de l'électricité produite par les installations photovoltaïques sur bâtiment de puissance inférieure ou égale à 500 kW en métropole, JORF of 4 June 2026, art. 8: the purchase tariff of the surplus is 1.1 c€ per kWh excluding VAT, indexed by 2 percent per year, for a contract of 20 years; art. 1: installations up to 9 kWc may only sell their surplus; the energy above 1600 hours times the peak power per year is not paid at this tariff.

sources.name: Bundesnetzagentur EEG feed-in tariffs 2026
sources.description: Bundesnetzagentur, EEG-Förderung und -Fördersätze, queried on 8 October 2026: the feed-in tariff for photovoltaic installations on buildings commissioned from 1 August to 31 December 2026 is 7.70 ct per kWh up to 10 kW with partial feed-in (12.22 ct per kWh with full feed-in), fixed for 20 years; the EEG values are net amounts.

sources.name: GSE guaranteed minimum prices 2026
sources.description: Gestore dei Servizi Energetici (GSE), Prezzi minimi garantiti per l'anno 2026, updated by ARERA on 29 January 2026 under deliberation 280/07: for photovoltaic installations up to 1 MW in the Ritiro Dedicato the guaranteed minimum price is 47.5 EUR per MWh for the first 1500000 kWh per year; if the hourly zonal market prices give more over the year, GSE pays these prices instead.
